wizard.installRun: Run this on the machine, as the user who runs the agents. It downloads and verifies colony, then walks you through the setup (dependencies, guard.yaml, service). While the repository is private it needs the GitHub CLI (gh) to be logged in.

platformNotes.linux: Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora: it installs the missing programs (git, tmux, bubblewrap) after you confirm. Logging in to the AI clients (claude, agy) is your job.
platformNotes.wsl: WSL needs systemd: if it is off, the installer turns it on, then `wsl --shutdown` in Windows is needed. On request it keeps WSL running after you log in to Windows.
platformNotes.macos: macOS has no sandbox yet: only full-access agents run on this machine. The guard runs as a launchd service.

emptyOwnBody: When a machine is given to you, it shows here, and you set your Claude login on it here.

access.notConfigured: none: the machine's guard.yaml has no claude_token_file
access.clearBody: The guard deletes the token file; the machine's Claude runs then use its user's own login, if any.
access.dialogBody: Your agents on this machine work with your own Claude subscription.
access.step1: On your own computer (not this server), open a terminal where Claude Code is installed.
access.step2: run it and sign in with your own subscription.
access.step3: Copy the token it prints and paste it here.
access.checking: The guard is checking the token (claude /usage); this can take a minute…
access.privacy: The token reaches only this machine's guard. The server never stores or logs it; it records only who set it and when.
